## One ecosystem, four packages

**vellum** is a family of R packages for drawing, built around a shared scene
model and a common design. The metaphor runs through the names: *vellum is the
parchment, vellumplot is the pen, and vellumwidget is the annotation revealed on
the page.*

| Package | Role | Analogue |
|---|---|---|
| [**vellum**](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellum/) | Low-level graphics backend — a retained scene graph, a unit/layout engine, and PNG/SVG/PDF rendering, all running in a Rust engine. | `grid` |
| [**vellumplot**](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/) | A declarative, pipe-first grammar of graphics that compiles an inspectable plot spec into a vellum scene. | `ggplot2` |
| [**vellumwidget**](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumwidget/) | Client-side interactive HTML widgets built from a vellum scene — hover, select, brush, zoom. No Shiny, no server. | `plotly` / `htmlwidgets` |
| [**vellumverse**](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumverse/) | A meta-package that installs and loads the whole ecosystem together. | `tidyverse` |

## What makes it different

- **A Rust backend.** The scene graph, layout solver, and renderers (raster,
  SVG, PDF) live in Rust via extendr. Output is deterministic and
  byte-stable across platforms — snapshot-testable graphics.
- **One scene, three formats.** The same scene renders identically to PNG, SVG,
  or PDF; geometry and text shaping stay consistent.
- **A real compiler, not a wrapper.** A vellumplot plot is a serializable spec.
  Nothing is drawn until it compiles: encodings resolve, scales train, the
  panel layout is measured, and guides and marks are emitted as vellum grobs.
- **A retained scene graph.** Because the scene is retained rather than drawn
  immediate-mode, elements carry data keys and bounding boxes — which is exactly
  what vellumwidget needs to wire up interactivity in the browser.
- **A modern paint model.** Gradients, tiling patterns, alpha/luminance masks,
  group opacity, and blend modes; plus built-in big-data aggregation with
  `datashade()` and hand-drawn ("sketch") rendering.

## Pipe-first, ggplot2-adjacent

If you know ggplot2 the vocabulary will feel familiar — `mark_point()`,
`scale_color_continuous()`, `facet_wrap()`, `theme_minimal()` — but plots are
composed with the native pipe `|>` rather than `+`, and aesthetics are plain
named arguments on each mark (no `aes()`):

```r
library(vellumplot)

vplot(mtcars) |>
  mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp) |>
  scale_color_continuous()
```

## About this gallery

Every example on this site is real, runnable code — rendered by vellumplot on
the vellum backend and frozen into the site so the deployment never needs to
rebuild the Rust engine. The site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org)
and styled to match the ecosystem's pkgdown pages (a parchment / sepia palette,
set in Spectral).

Source lives at [r-vellum/vellumgallery](https://github.com/r-vellum/vellumgallery).
